title: Sundial Ware - security readiness and deployment options
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment
summary: Initial security-intake discovery with Sundial Ware focused on compliance posture (SOC2+ISO roadmap), identity & access (SSO/SAML, SCIM), RBAC model, audit/logging retention needs, encryption and key management options, and deployment constraints (preference for VPC or dedicated). The team asked for SOC2 report, diagrams of private control plane, and an expected pilot/benchmark plan. Agreed next steps: send security pack, propose pilot scope and capacity, schedule SE deep-dive for KMS and networking.
next_steps: Alex to share SOC2 report and security whitepaper by 2026-03-18
Maya to propose pilot architecture and resource estimate by 2026-03-22
Customer to provide data residency and retention policy doc by 2026-03-20
action_items: Alex Mercer: send SOC2 Type II report + encryption/KMS FAQ (due 2026-03-18)
Maya Chen: draft pilot blueprint (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and expected latency/cost tradeoffs (due 2026-03-22)
Priya Rao / Sundial: share data classification & retention matrix (due 2026-03-20)
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-16 15:30 PDT | Duration 42m | Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CTO, Sundial), Priya Rao (Head of Security, Sundial), Samir Patel (Platform Lead)

00:00 Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, we really appreciate you taking the time. quick roll call?
00:07 Jordan: yeah jordan here.
00:09 Priya: priya here.
00:12 Samir: samir on the line.
00:15 Alex: perfect. so goal today's to run through security constraints and deployment options — hosted, dedicated, private — and what you need for SOC2/ISO alignment.

02:03 Maya: quick note from our side, we often see customers start hosted for dev and small prod then move dedicated or private for regulated workloads. but we're flexible.

03:21 Priya: the big asks up front are SOC2 Type II evidence, SSO / SAML support with SCIM for provisioning, RBAC we can map to our internal roles, audit logs retention for 7 years for some teams, and KMS integration. also, does redwood support customer-managed keys?

03:45 Alex: yep we can share SOC2 report, and we do offer customer managed keys for private deployments and a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flow for some dedicated customers. small nuance: hosted has managed KMS unless you move to private or dedicated with specific entitlements.

05:12 Jordan: timeline wise we have to present to the compliance committee in 3 weeks, so we need artifacts and a pilot plan that proves no sensitive data leakage.

06:04 Maya: for data leak concerns we use prefix caching and model routing, but we can enable strict request-level logs and masked payloads. audit logs can be exported to your SIEM via syslog or cloud logging sinks. retention is configurable in private deployments, hosted is typically 90 days but enterprise add-on can extend.

07:20 Priya: 90 days is not enough for us for the clinical logs, we need 7 years for certain audit trails. is there a legal/technical blocker to that in dedicated?

07:44 Maya: no technical blocker in dedicated/private — you can retain logs in your own bucket or your VPC. hosted can be extended with data retention add-ons but it's more of an enterprise contract discussion.

09:10 Samir: what's the SSO story, we use Okta, want SAML + SCIM for auto-provisioning. also need role sync so product roles map to our RBAC groups.

09:28 Alex: Okta is supported. SAML SSO works on hosted and dedicated; SCIM provisioning is typically available for enterprise tenants. RBAC can be configured so that teams map to groups and entitlements.

11:02 Priya: encryption at rest — do you support envelope encryption with our KMS (AWS KMS/HSM)? and what about auditability around key usage?

11:18 Maya: we support envelope encryption and can integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSMs for private. For dedicated we offer a customer-managed KMS option. Key usage logs can be forwarded; if you use your KMS, key rotation/audit stays in your account and you control logs.

13:50 Jordan: can we get network diagrams for the private control plane? we need to show isolation model to our security architects.

14:05 Alex: absolutely, we'll send VPC diagrams and recommended firewall rules. for private deployments we ship a customer-managed control plane that sits in your VPC and talks back over a secure mTLS channel to Redwood ops endpoints; we can redact operational endpoints in the diagram per NDA.

16:30 Priya: SOC2 vs ISO — which certs do you have today? and how often are reports updated?

16:45 Alex: we maintain SOC2 Type II and are in the process of certifying ISO 27001 this year; SOC2 is updated annually and we can provide the latest report and the summary of controls. for ISO we'll share scope and expected timeline.

18:05 Samir: curious about audit logs schema — what's captured? request metadata, tokens, prompt/response content?

18:18 Maya: by default we capture request metadata, timestamps, model id, route, and anonymized input hashes. content logging is opt-in; for enterprise pilots we can enable full request/response logging but that is stored per your retention policy and can be routed to your storage.

20:10 Jordan: ok that helps. about data residency — we have EU customers so we'd prefer EU-only processing and storage. is region pinning supported?

20:23 Alex: yes region pinning is supported for both hosted (enterprise regional tenancy) and for dedicated/private — you can run in a EU region or in your on-prem environment.

22:55 Priya: what about RBAC for model access specifically — we want certain teams to be able to query smaller models but only the ML team can call the large LLMs because of cost and data exposure.

23:12 Maya: that's a common pattern. we have per-route and per-model policies you can bind to roles. you can also set quotas and guardrails. For Dedicated/Private you get more granular CPU/GPU tenancy and policies.

25:00 Priya: any background checks on ops engineers, do you offer contractual controls around who can access customer environments?

25:12 Alex: yes enterprise contracts include access controls, background checks for privileged ops staff, and two-person review for sensitive actions. we can provide an outline in the security pack.

27:40 Jordan: performance — we may run low-latency inference for chat features. how do you handle fallback if a region is saturated? we can't have user-facing outages.

28:00 Maya: we support smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants and can do multi-region replication for state. for critical flows we recommend dedicated pools or private installs behind a canary that fails over to dedicated-hosted route.

30:10 Samir: cost question — is dedicated billed as reserved capacity? what's the minimum?

30:22 Alex: dedicated is reserved pools with monthly commitments; we usually size pilots small and provide a burst path. we'll share a reference pricing sheet.

32:05 Priya: one more on logs — chain of custody for logs and tamper evidence, can we support WORM or append-only storage?

32:22 Maya: yes if you store logs in your own bucket you can configure WORM retention, and we also provide signed audit entries for certain event types.

34:00 Jordan: ok let's talk immediate deliverables. we'll need: SOC2 report, network/control plane diagram, KMS integration notes, pilot blueprint and an estimated cost for a 2-week benchmark.

34:18 Alex: yes that's aligned. I'll send the SOC2 and security pack. Maya will send pilot blueprint. Priya will provide their retention and data classification doc.

36:12 Priya: are there any blockers on Redwood side for us doing an on-prem private deployment? our security team prefers air-gapped for some data flows.

36:26 Maya: we do support an on-prem private package; fully air-gapped installs are possible but require professional services and lead time for packaging. We'll outline requirements in the blueprint.

38:40 Jordan: outstanding competitor question — we evaluated Anthropic earlier; main difference we saw was deployment flexibility and cost predictability. can you highlight the main differentiation in the docs?

38:56 Alex: yep we'll include a short competitive positioning note but keep it factual.

40:05 (Overlap) Priya: thanks all, this was helpful.
40:10 Alex: recap and next steps: send SOC2 + security pack by Thu, pilot blueprint by next Monday, customer to share retention matrix by Friday, and schedule the deeper SE KMS/networking call for next week.
40:28 Jordan: we'll loop in procurement after we review the docs.
40:35 Alex: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links.

End.
